originalTeachingCards.title: Read two actions happening together
originalTeachingCards.body: An imperfective verbal adverb describes an accompanying action. In the supplied читая письмо, он улыбался, he was reading the letter while he smiled. Reading and smiling overlap: simultaneous means during the same interval as the main predicate. The main verb places this example in the past; читая does not independently mean absolute present time. The retained examples думая and учась illustrate imperfective verbal-adverb forms. An isolated form cannot establish the tense of an absent main verb.

originalTeachingCards.title: Keep the two actions with the same person
originalTeachingCards.body: In читая письмо, он улыбался, The pronoun he is the explicit main-clause subject. The reader and the person smiling are the same person. The verbal adverb supplies an accompanying action by that subject, not an action by a second unrelated person. Identify the main verb and its subject before deciding who performs the accompanying action. These checks recognize timing and shared subject in the supplied construction; they do not demonstrate forming an unfamiliar verbal adverb or judging every possible literary use.

additionalExistingCard.title: Read the retained literary timing context
additionalExistingCard.body: The retained paragraph introduces Павел Сергеич Вязовский as the actor. отдыхал читая — Reading accompanies resting; the same person performs both actions in this supplied episode. The source marks читать as imperfective. simultaneous with the main predicate describes timing relative to the main predicate in this clause. The actor is supplied by the paragraph, not inserted into a new Russian sentence. This is an exact clause selection with source punctuation and spacing preserved. Compare the independent letter sentence already taught: it keeps its original relative-time and shared-subject reading. The same literary episode appears later in reading practice; this is not unseen evidence, a rule that fixes absolute tense, or unrestricted formation/production mastery.

originalTeachingCards.title: Read the completed action before the main action
originalTeachingCards.body: A perfective verbal adverb normally presents an action completed before the main action in this taught construction. Anterior means earlier relative to that action. The retained сказав and научившись illustrate these forms; their labels alone do not fix an absolute past tense. Read the accompanying main predicate to establish the sentence time.

originalTeachingCards.title: Earlier does not necessarily mean past
originalTeachingCards.body: In написав письмо, она отправит его завтра, she will send the letter tomorrow after writing it. The writing precedes the future sending: anterior to a future main action is the matching description. The sentence does not require the writing to have happened before the present moment. The pronoun she names the main subject, and the writer and sender are the same person. An absolute present label loses the relative timing; assigning a different subject loses the supplied construction.

originalTeachingCards.title: Recognize the retained form without inventing a formation rule
originalTeachingCards.body: The retained войдя illustrates another perfective verbal-adverb form with an action normally anterior to its main predicate. It does not by itself identify a main subject or an absolute sentence tense. Compare the supplied forms and read their complete contexts when available. This small example set supplies recognition practice, not a complete productive algorithm for unlisted verbs.
